CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports cough beginning approximately one week ago with production of yellow sputum. Reports feeling worse over the last two days. Denies fever but reports feeling warm without having taken temperature. Denies chills. Reports feeling achy at times. Denies shortness of breath. Reports congestion with drainage down throat and bilateral sinus pressure. No other household members are sick. Patient works as a teacher.

Patient also reports that earlier today while coughing, he fell down approximately 4-5 stairs and twisted his right knee. Pain is mostly on the inside of the knee. Able to walk with a slight limp. Denies knee giving out. Able to bend and straighten the knee. Taking over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold symptoms with minimal relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Fever: Denies fever but feels warm. Has not taken temperature.
Chills: Denies.
General: Reports feeling achy at times.
Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath. Productive cough with yellow sputum.
ENT: Congestion with throat drainage and bilateral sinus pressure.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension.
Diabetes.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily.
Metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
Dayquil over-the-counter for cough and cold.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupation: Teacher. Denies being a sports fan. Wife in good health.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62, Heart Rate in the 80s, Oxygen Saturation 97% on room air.

Facial Exam: Bilateral maxillary sinus pain to palpation.

Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of bilateral nasal turbinates with yellow discharge.

Throat Exam: Uvula midline. No erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space.

Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy.

Lung Exam: Coarse rhonchi bilaterally that clear with cough.

Cardiac Exam: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmur.

Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation. Decreased flexion and extension. Ecchymosis to right medial knee. No effusion.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Cough/Upper Respiratory Infection with Mild Bronchitis - Viral Syndrome: Continue over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to help clear phlegm. No antibiotics at this time. Patient to call if symptoms worsen; chest x-ray to be considered at that time to rule out pneumonia.

2. Right Medial Collateral Ligament Strain: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Refer to physical therapy to strengthen surrounding muscles. Order right knee x-ray to rule out bone injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel.

4. Diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c. Advise patient to monitor sugar intake and report blood sugars through patient portal.
